To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CTGF and IGT1 are both expressed at different stages of the neoplastic process of GI NE cells and that CTGF expression may correlate with the stage and the size of GNETs, but only in type I ECL cell carcinoid tumours.

1) CTGF was expressed by a proportion of NE tumour cells of normal GI mucosa, but not by ECL cells, and 2) it was absent in the majority of poorly differentiated carcinomas of the stomach and the midgut, but present in most well-differentiated gastric carcinoids and in all but a single midgut NET, suggesting that CTGF may be involved in their neoplastic transformation
CTGF and IGC1 are expressed in the GI NE cells and their tumours.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible involvement of CTGF and/or IGF1 in the development of GI NE cells and NETs.
the expression of CTGF in normal and neoplasic GI NE cells and the possible correlation with clinico-pathological variables.
the expression of CTGF, a novel growth factor, and IGF1, a known growth factor, in GI NE cells, as well as in the foci ECL cell hyperpla-sia and in the various types of GNETs and midgut NE tumours.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CTGF is expressed in a proportion (but not all) of GI NETs, whereas IGF-1 is expressed in all.
both CTGF expression in GNETs and IGF1 expression in GI NETs may be useful as prognostic markers.
both CTGF (in well-differentiated tumours) and IGF-1 (in both well and poorly differentiated tumours) may play a role in the development and/or progression of GI NETs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both CTGF, which may be a marker of tumour aggressiveness in GNETs, and IGF1, which is a marker of tumorigenesis in GI NETs, may be involved in tumour development and progression.
the CTGF and IGC1 may be involved at different stages of the neoplastic development of GI NE tumours, but CTGF is mainly expressed in advanced tumours.
both CTGF (mainly in ECL-CC) and IGF-1 are involved in the neoplatic transformation of GI neuroendocrine cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CTGF is expressed by the majority of midgut NE cells and by some GNETs.
both CTGF expression and IGF1 levels are increased in GI NE cells, suggesting that they may be involved in tumour progression.
CTGF and IGC1 are involved in the pathogenesis of GI NETs, and that they may be useful biomarkers in the diagnosis and management of GI NETs.
